stem: A 79 year old patient, with a history of AF, presents to ED complaining of sudden onset severe abdominal pain. Imaging shows occlusion of the superior mesenteric artery. Which of the following structures is most likely affected:
fact: The SMA supplies the midgut, including jejunum and ileum.
finding: NCBI confirms jejunal and ileal supply by SMA.

stem: Posteriorly the spleen lies in the region of which of the following:
fact: The spleen projects posteriorly over ribs 9–11 and follows the contour of rib 10.
finding: Source explanation and standard surface anatomy support ribs 9–11.

stem: The ductus deferens is derived from which of the following structures:
fact: The ductus deferens continues from the tail of the epididymis.

stem: A patient presents following a fall. Imaging shows damage to the L1 nerve root. Which of the following muscles are most likely to be affected:
options: Transversus abdominis and rectus abdominis muscles
Rectus abdominis and external oblique muscles
Transversus abdominis and internal oblique muscles
fact: The ilioinguinal nerve from L1 contributes motor supply to transversus abdominis and internal oblique.
mnemonic: L1 ilioinguinal: internal oblique and transversus.
finding: NCBI confirms origin and motor distribution.

stem: The cutaneous supply of the scrotum is derived primarily from which of the following spinal nerve roots.
fact: Scrotal sensation has mixed roots, primarily L1 and S2–S3 in the source explanation.
finding: NCBI confirms L1 ilioinguinal contribution; the source explains S2–S3 contributions. Mixed-root caveat retained.

stem: The kidneys extend between which of the following vertebral levels:
fact: In the supine position, kidneys extend approximately from T12 to L3, with variation from respiration and position.
finding: NCBI supports the approximate T12–L3 range.

stem: The body of the pancreas lies at which of the following vertebral levels:
fact: The pancreatic body lies in the transpyloric plane at vertebra L1.
finding: Source explanation and NCBI pancreatic anatomy support L1.

stem: Regarding the uterine tubes, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: The uterine tubes open into the peritoneal cavity lateral to the ovaries.
Each uterine tube is approximately 5 cm long.
The opening of the uterine tube is formed by the ampulla.
The infundibulum is the narrowest part of the uterine tube.
Ectopic pregnancies occur most commonly in the isthmus of the uterine tube.
fact: Uterine tubes open into the peritoneal cavity lateral to the ovaries; the source gives 10–12 cm length, isthmus as narrowest, and ampulla as commonest ectopic site.
mnemonic: Tube opens laterally; ampulla is the common ectopic site.
finding: NCBI supports fallopian-tube anatomy; source-specific teaching retained.

stem: A 79 year old man presents to ED complaining of fever and left sided abdominal and back pain. Imaging reveals a large perinephric abscess. Which of the following most likely describes the fluid location:
options: Between the renal cortex and the renal capsule
Between the renal capsule and the perinephric fat
Between the renal capsule and the renal fascia
Between the renal fascia and the paranephric fat
fact: Perinephric fat lies between the renal capsule and renal fascia; a perinephric abscess occupies this compartment.
finding: Source explanation directly defines the compartment.

stem: A patient is brought to ED following abdominal trauma. Your consultant performs a FAST scan in the department and identifies fluid in Morison's pouch. Where is Morison's pouch located:
fact: Morison's pouch is the posterior right subhepatic space between the liver and right kidney and is a dependent peritoneal recess.
finding: NCBI supports the hepatorenal recess as a dependent peritoneal space; source explanation supplies exact relation.
